how.title: How it works
how.subtitle: Total transparency. No magic, no servers, no tricks.
how.step1Body: Everything happens in your browser. When you press Generate, BG KeyForge calls the Web Crypto API (crypto.getRandomValues), a cryptographically secure source available in every modern browser.
how.step2Body: We use rejection sampling: random values that would produce bias when mapped to the alphabet are discarded. Every character in the alphabet has exactly the same probability.
how.step3Body: When you require at least one character of each type, we shuffle the result with a Fisher-Yates fed by crypto.getRandomValues. No predictable patterns at the beginning.
how.step4Body: Passwords never reach an endpoint. We don't use localStorage, cookies, logs or analytics that can see them. Refresh the page and they cease to exist.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.subtitle: What we DON'T do matters as much as what we do.

items.noSave: We don't save your passwords anywhere.
items.noSee: We can't see them: they never reach a server.
items.noSend: They are not sent over the internet, ever.
items.noDb: We don't use a database: there's nothing to leak.
items.noAccount: No account, registration or email required.
items.noHistory: We don't record history or generation telemetry.

privacy.footnote: You can verify this by going offline: the generator still works exactly the same.

tips.title: Digital security tips
tips.subtitle: A great password is only the first step.

manager.title: Use a password manager
manager.body: A manager remembers long, unique passwords for you, autofills them and encrypts them with a master key.

noReuse.title: Don't reuse passwords
noReuse.body: If a site is breached, every account sharing that password is exposed. One unique password per service.

twoFactor.title: Enable two-factor authentication
twoFactor.body: Prefer TOTP apps (Authy, 1Password, Aegis) or hardware security keys (FIDO2) over SMS.

passkeys.title: Use passkeys whenever you can
passkeys.body: Passkeys replace passwords with public-key cryptography: nothing to remember, nothing to phish.

noShare.title: Don't share them via chat or email
noShare.body: Those channels are often archived in plaintext. Use the secure sharing feature of your password manager.

noPlain.title: Don't store them in unencrypted files
noPlain.body: A .txt, Notes app or open Word doc is an easy target. If you must store them, encrypt the file or use a manager.

rotate.title: Rotate leaked passwords
rotate.body: Check haveibeenpwned.com with your email. If any appeared in a breach, regenerate it here and change it now.

update.title: Keep your browser and OS updated
update.body: Browser vulnerabilities can expose any data. Enable automatic updates.

save.q: Does BG KeyForge save my passwords?
save.a: No. There's no database, no localStorage, no cookies that hold them. They exist only in this tab's memory while you keep it open.

sent.q: Are passwords sent over the internet?
sent.a: Never. Generation happens entirely in your browser via the Web Crypto API. You can disconnect from the internet and verify it.

length.a: For critical services that accept long passwords (managers, email, banking), 100 characters provide a huge margin against brute force. For sites with limits, lower the value.

txt.a: Only if you understand the risks. A .txt file is not encrypted. Use it as a temporary step to move keys into a manager and then securely delete it.

any.q: Can I use these passwords in any account?
any.a: Yes, although some services limit length or certain symbols. If a password is rejected, try a shorter length or enable 'Avoid problematic symbols'.

noSymbols.q: What if a site doesn't accept symbols?
noSymbols.a: Disable symbols and increase the length (e.g. 32+). With enough letters and numbers you keep very high entropy.
